summary: The unit test suite (bump-version.bats) provides solid coverage of core functionality: version parsing, bump precedence (breaking>feat>fix), both VERSION and package.json formats, prefix preservation, error cases, and changelog generation. However, coverage gaps include: scopes in commit messages (e.g. `feat(scope):`), malformed commit formats, empty commits files, case variations in BREAKING-CHANGE footers, and whitespace edge cases. The workflow structure tests are basic but functional. The act-harness E2E tests are well-architected (isolated repos, exact value assertions, job success checks) but critically incomplete: they reference fixture directories (fixtures/minor/, fixtures/major/, fixtures/package/) and a .actrc file that are not provided in the code, making these tests unable to run as-is. Additionally, only 3 E2E scenarios are defined when the complexity warrants 5-6+. The changelog test checks grouping but doesn't verify that new entries correctly prepend to existing content. Test design is clean (good isolation, clear names, proper setup/teardown) but undermined by missing dependencies. Would catch major regressions in happy path but miss subtle bugs and boundary conditions.
